versions.note: First version. Reference = average of 11–13 Oct as the feed stood on 14 Oct; stakers' share 85%; supply tuning 3.0 estimated from two press figures; market bet ~$100M on $9K traded. 64 links audited, 23 corrections from the draft.

Same method, inputs re-read on 17 Oct: reference = average of 14–16 Oct; stakers' share 91%; revenue so far $55.2M; supply tuning 4.0 read from the live contract's high-water mark; market bet ~$200M on $132K traded. Method unchanged.

Same method, inputs re-read on 20 Oct: reference = average of 17–19 Oct, the three days after the rush broke ($0.90M, $2.34M, $1.91M); stakers' share 89%; revenue so far $60.33M; supply tuning 4.2 read from the contract's high-water mark; market bet ~$25M on $285K traded (was ~$200M). Method unchanged; the payout bar never doubled.

Method change: the timelocked upgrade went live on 21 Oct, so supply now follows the contract's new mint rule (each $1M of loss mints 0.110% of supply, no ceiling), read from the contract. Inputs re-read on 27 Oct: reference = average of 24–26 Oct ($1.34M, $0.07M, $0.63M), down 60% again; stakers' share 95%; mint basis $3.3 per $1 of revenue since the upgrade; market bet ~$25M, with every strike now under 50%. The payout bar is still $5M.

Same method as Version 4, inputs re-read on 10 Nov: reference = average of 7–9 Nov ($0.06M, $0.75M, $0.51M), down 36%; stakers' share 97%; mint basis $3.7 per $1 of revenue over the 19 days since the upgrade; supply 9.28B. The payout bar is still $5M and the queue $0; the market bet stays at most ~$25M. Ran a week late: the 3 Nov run hit the desk's usage limit.

Same method as Versions 4 and 5, inputs re-read on 11 Nov, one day after Version 5 (a key date: Version 2's base-case stop line): reference = average of 8–10 Nov ($0.75M, $0.51M, $1.00M), up 72% because one day changed (10 Nov's $1.00M in, 7 Nov's $0.06M out); stakers' share 97%; mint basis $3.5 per $1 of revenue over the 20 days since the upgrade; supply 9.30B. The payout bar is still $5M and the queue $0; the market bet stays at most ~$25M. An upgrade (a new Exchange, contract set 3) was queued the same morning and can run from 12 Nov; it sets neither the bar nor the mint constant.

timeline.title: Launch
timeline.text: Trading opens with $138M deposited by 11,465 wallets. Day one: $25.2M of trader losses, $24M paid to stakers.

timeline.title: The rush fades
timeline.text: Day two revenue $2.6M, down 90% from launch day. The question the study asks: how much of this survives?

timeline.title: Best day since launch
timeline.text: $7.49M of revenue, #2 in crypto behind Tether. Revenue is rising, not decaying, a week in.

timeline.title: Payout bar doubles
timeline.text: After 18:45 UTC the pool keeps the next $5M of losses before stakers see extra payouts. The page marks the call itself from tomorrow's contract read.

timeline.title: Pool slips under the bar
timeline.text: At 10:47 UTC the house pool read $4.83M, under the $5M bar, so stakers have had only the 1% win fee since about midnight UTC. About $172K of net trader losses tops it up again; the bar doubles to $10M after 18:45 UTC. First tell against the base case. One quiet Saturday is not new evidence.

timeline.title: Bar did not double
timeline.text: The 18 Oct contract read still showed the payout bar at $5M, so the page marked the 17 Oct call missed by itself. No official word found. The pool kept touching the bar and sweeping to stakers, so payouts never paused: the 17 Oct tell was a dip between sweeps, not a pause.

timeline.title: The rush has broken
timeline.text: 17–19 Oct closed at $0.90M, $2.34M and $1.91M of revenue a day, down 73% from 14–16 Oct. Open bets fell from $569M to $315M; PAPER minted a day fell from 313M to about 130M.

timeline.title: Upgrade live; the house gives back $2.7M
timeline.text: At 22:00 UTC the timelocked upgrade went live, unannounced as such (the team posted a five-minute "maintenance"): each $1M of loss now mints 0.110% of PAPER's supply, with no ceiling, and trades closed within a few basis points pay a fee band. Earlier that day house money fell from $10.0M to $7.3M while the bets leaned 18.4× the house money, and revenue was $177K. Two calls marked themselves: the throttle tell missed, the mint rate under 10 PAPER per $1 hit (on the old curve, hours before it was retired).

timeline.title: Quietest day yet
timeline.text: Revenue $72.8K, the lowest closed day since launch; money on platform $32.3M, under a quarter of the $138M deposited before launch. The first builder codes went live that evening. The payout bar still read $5M.

timeline.title: Best day in ten
timeline.text: Revenue $2.02M, the highest closed day since 18 Oct and 34 times 27 Oct's $59.9K; stakers got 96% of it. One day moved the three-day average 2.7×, the swing the reference question is about.

timeline.title: Quietest days yet
timeline.text: Revenue $19.3K on 31 Oct and $19.8K on 1 Nov, the two lowest closed days since launch. The pool read under the $5M bar on both days' contract reads, and stakers got 50% of revenue, the fee split alone. Money on platform $28.3M.

timeline.title: Version 5 slips a week
timeline.text: The scheduled re-run did not start: the desk hit its weekly usage limit (the 3–5 Nov daily checks too). The daily data job kept writing, so no reading was lost; Version 5 ran on 10 Nov.

timeline.title: House money at its low
timeline.text: The daily read put house money at $5.91M (pool $3.19M, reserve $2.72M), the lowest on file, while the bets leaned 6.6× the house money. The queue stayed at $0, and a day later the house was back at $8.17M.

timeline.title: Best day since 29 Oct
timeline.text: Revenue $1.00M, the highest closed day since 29 Oct's $2.02M, 97% of it to stakers. It replaced 7 Nov's $60K in the three-day reference, which rose 72% overnight: the swing the reference question (BOARD 18) is about. House money read $8.52M, the queue $0.

timeline.title: Upgrade queued: contract set 3
timeline.text: At 00:47 UTC the team queued a seven-call batch in the timelock: a new Exchange (by the docs' own definition, contract set 3), PaperStaking and BatchExecutor code, idle USDC lent on HyperCore with the interest to stakers, and a donateToLp path with the team's multisig as donor; staked-PAPER transfers to whitelisted contracts are coded but "unused for now". Nothing in it sets the payout bar or the mint constant. Its first post since 25 Oct announced it. It can run from 12 Nov 00:47 UTC.

timeline.title: Upgrade can run
timeline.text: The queued batch can execute from 00:47 UTC. The daily read then shows whether the bar, the mint constant or the dashboard's readings moved; a version follows within a week (Version 7, 17 Nov).

timeline.title: Version 7
timeline.text: Weekly re-run. Does revenue hold near $0.6M a day (seven-day average $0.59M on 10 Nov), and has the payout bar or the mint constant moved in the timelock?

timeline.title: $138M money check
timeline.text: The bull case needs money on the platform back above the pre-launch deposits.
